flows.name: Persist the automatic-generation database owner
steps: Read back function signature, ACL, cron command, and removed prerequisite
flows.expectedOutcome: The database can create a first automatic period through a project-scoped service-role call while preserving the global cron

flows.name: Protect calendar-month boundaries
steps: Run focused first-day and last-day recurrence tests
Cover ordinary and leap February plus 30-day and 31-day months
flows.expectedOutcome: Monthly anchors do not drift across calendar-month lengths

flows.name: Fail conflicting schedules loudly
steps: Exercise the settings API conflict response
Review exact and partial-overlap rollback contracts
flows.expectedOutcome: Conflicts preserve the prior schedule and return an actionable error

flows.name: Save and reload the production schedule
steps: Save the monthly schedule from an authenticated Nexcom route
Reload the route and confirm Monthly plus exactly one BP-001
Capture the final desktop and mobile dialogs
flows.expectedOutcome: The first period is created idempotently and the month-boundary controls remain usable at both breakpoints

claims.description: The reviewed migration is applied and the function, ACL, cron, and removed prerequisite were read back
Focused regression tests cover first/last calendar-day behavior without month-length drift
Independent code and database reviews approve the release candidate
The authenticated production save succeeds, reload persists one period, and final desktop/mobile screenshots pass
